messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected — inference-prod: sustained throttle events and queue depth surge across rtx-pool-3 starting ~10:40 UTC. Auto-escalation: paging on-call.

maria: I’m on it. seeing tokens/sec spike and queue_depth jump from 120 -> 820 in ~6m. Throttle events spiking to ~6% of requests (429s).

kevin: Confirmed from logs — a batch job spilled a bunch of long-context requests. Not a deploy.

ashley: Customer impact: 3 customers reported degraded latency and retries, one reported partial failures in async-infer pipeline. SRE oncall emailed PG with customer list.

raj: Oncall here. Quick mitigation options: 1) bump autoscale target for rtx-pool-3 to allow 2x capacity, 2) evasive action: enable temporary per-account rate limiting for heavy accounts, 3) fallback routing to rtx-pool-1 (less loaded).

maria: Spawning scale action now (manual scale + autoscaler warmup).

deploy-bot: Manual scale initiated by maria: set desired_instances=48 -> executing.

kevin: While scaling, we should apply a quick alert tuning to reduce noisy pages — current queue_depth alert fires too early w/ short debounce. Suggest change: increase evaluation_period from 1m -> 3m and add rate-of-change condition.

note: current alert definition for queue_depth:
```
ALERT: high-queue-depth
WHEN: queue_depth > 300
FOR: 1m
```

maria: Agreed. Operationally we still want a page if customer impact > 5% requests or error budget is burned. Propose adding a compound condition: page only if (queue_depth > 500 for 3m) OR (throttle_rate > 4% for 1m) OR (tokens/sec > X and error_rate > Y).

ashley: Can we add a non-paging severity for the intermediate case? E.g., PagerDuty P2 for 300-500 queue depth with high tokens/sec but no customer visible errors.

raj: Yep. Implementation plan: create two alerts — high-queue-critical (page) and high-queue-warning (no page). Warning posts to #eng-sre and to ops-runbook channel.

kevin: Also suggest introducing a smoothing metric: queue_depth_rate = derivative(queue_depth) and use that to catch sudden spikes. That will prevent small oscillations from firing alerts.

maria: Scaling finished, instances up in ~90s. Throttle rate fell from 6% -> 1.2% after warmup. Queue depth trending down.

ashley: Customer outage status: degraded -> partial degradation, customers back to retries but latency still high for longer contexts. We've notified 2 affected customers and provided ETA for full mitigation.

raj: For postmortem and future prevention we need:
- dashboard: tokens/sec per-account heatmap, queue_depth per-pool with rate-of-change panel, throttle_events timeline correlated with model size and sequence_len.
- alerts: update queue_depth alerts as discussed, add tokens/sec spike alert aggregated and per-account top-k, and add a throttle_events escalation when >3% for 2m.

kevin: Proposed alert edits (exact):
```
ALERT: high-queue-critical
WHEN: queue_depth > 700
FOR: 3m
ACTION: page P1

ALERT: high-queue-warning
WHEN: queue_depth > 300 AND queue_depth < 700
FOR: 5m
ACTION: notify #eng-sre (no page)

ALERT: tokens-spike
WHEN: increase(tokens/sec, 2m) > 2x baseline AND top_account_tokens > 25% total
FOR: 1m
ACTION: notify oncall + ops

ALERT: throttle-escalation
WHEN: throttle_rate > 3% FOR 2m
ACTION: page
```

maria: One more: add an override flag for incidents where we intentionally route traffic to smaller model variants — that should suppress paging for token-spike-only scenarios.

ashley: I'll open a dashboard ticket and include required panels + mockups. Also adding a playbook section to runbook: steps to identify heavy accounts, temp rate limit, fallback routing, and safe-scale procedure.

raj: Who will own alert rollout? I can do the alert config change now (I'll test in staging first).

kevin: I’ll own dashboard + query templates and add example KQL/PromQL snippets to runbook.

maria: I'll coordinate customer comms and curate the impacted account list for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident update — status: mitigated -> partial remediation complete. Throttle rate 1.1% (down from 6%), queue depth 140.

ashley: Quick follow-up: when we change alerts, ensure we keep the existing history/annotations so we can correlate older incidents. Don't delete old alert IDs; create new ones with references.

raj: Will do. I’ll create a PR in infra-alerts with the changes, include test alerting rules, and tag everyone for review.

maria: Thanks all. Addendum: we should consider adding autoscaler headroom profiling (preferred instance buffer) so the autoscaler doesn't react from zero and we avoid warm-up spikes. Agenda item for next SRE retro. :thumbsup:
